idea.why: Two independent source branches, one specialist reasoner per source with a strict bucketing contract, then a single editor whose only job is composing. Fetch, reason, compose and deliver are cleanly separated and no concern is smeared. Soft spot is interpreting presents as an emailed body rather than a served page.

structure.why: Purpose-built types throughout, eleven nodes proportionate, no Code node reimplementing something native. Mild criticism: none of the agents attach tools or memory, so they are chains dressed as agents, and the fence-stripping regex patches a constraint the editor prompt should have enforced.

connections.why: The trigger genuinely fans out rather than serialising two unrelated fetches, each branch chains only its real dependencies, and the streams rejoin at a barrier that exists precisely because both must finish first. The wiring is hard to improve on.

answer.why: End to end it delivers, with information genuinely sorted into buckets, a chronological timeline, overlaps and the largest free block. Held back because a full document with a media query is a poor fit for an email body, where most clients drop the responsive rules the layout depends on.

appraisal: Finds the shape the brief actually implies rather than the first that compiles: a true fan-out, one specialist per source with tightly scoped output contracts, a wait-for-all barrier, and a single editor that owns presentation. The robustness details are not accidental, with explicit empty-input instructions so a quiet inbox still produces a briefing instead of a dead branch. What it gets wrong is the last mile: the editor emits a standalone document with a media query, then that document is stuffed into a mail body where the responsive stacking will be partly stripped, and a regex strips fences a stricter constraint should have prevented. A knowledgeable user would fix delivery first, either serving it from a webhook or rewriting the prompt to emit email-safe table-and-inline-style HTML.
